title: IonQ Collaborates with CMC Microsystems to Expand Cloud Quantum Access Across Canada - Quantum Computing Report
gist: IonQ signed a non-binding MOU with CMC Microsystems to become an official cloud quantum access provider within Canada's $217M CAD FABrIC Quantum Computing Sandbox, giving Canadian academics and SMEs up to $100k per project in credits to run algorithms on IonQ trapped-ion hardware.

themes.theme: Canada market access via national sandbox

insights.claim: IonQ signed a Memorandum of Understanding with CMC Microsystems to integrate its commercial quantum systems into Canada's FABrIC Quantum Computing Sandbox, designating IonQ as an official cloud quantum access provider for Canadian researchers and SMEs.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Embeds IonQ hardware in a government-funded national program, expanding its addressable Canadian user base through an official channel.
insights.quote: The non-binding framework designates IonQ as an official cloud quantum access provider, enabling Canadian academic researchers, post-secondary institutions, and small-to-medium enterprises (SMEs) to execute algorithms on IonQ hardware.

insights.claim: The agreement is a non-binding framework led by IonQ Vice President of Global Strategy Lisa Lambert and CMC Microsystems CEO Gordon Harling.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: MOU status means the commercial upside is contingent on later binding commitments and actual project uptake.

insights.claim: The FABrIC Quantum Computing Sandbox is managed by CMC Microsystems and backed by the Canadian government's $217 million CAD FABrIC initiative funded via the Strategic Response Fund, providing direct cloud credits up to $100,000 per project plus technical engineering support.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Public credits subsidize demand for commercial quantum access, effectively de-risking early customer adoption for IonQ.
insights.quote: backed by the Canadian government's $217 million CAD FABrIC initiative (funded via the Strategic Response Fund), the Quantum Computing Sandbox provides direct cloud credits up to $100,000 per project alongside technical engineering support.

insights.claim: Participating teams can deploy algorithms across IonQ's trapped-ion processors, including its high-fidelity generation architectures, targeting quantum chemistry, materials science, financial modeling, and logistics optimization.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Broad application targeting positions IonQ hardware for diverse Canadian use-case discovery.

insights.claim: Under the Quantum Computing Sandbox terms, all intellectual property generated by researchers and companies during sandbox projects remains entirely the property of the participating developers, with no IP claims held by CMC Microsystems or platform providers.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Developer-retained IP lowers the barrier for commercial SMEs to participate and build defensible products.
insights.quote: all intellectual property (IP) generated by researchers and companies during sandbox projects remains entirely the property of the participating developers, with no IP claims held by CMC Microsystems or platform providers.
